title: Stalk order along a boundary hypersurface
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $I,D$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves, and $x\in X$. Use their stalk ideals of [def-trf-marked-ideal-order] and ordinary ideal powers [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers]. Define the boundary order $\operatorname{ord}_{D,x}I$ to be zero if $x\notin V(D)$, and otherwise $\sup\{v\in\mathbf N:I_x\subseteq D_x^v\}\in\mathbf N\cup\{\infty\}$. Thus a zero stalk ideal has infinite boundary order at a point on the boundary, and boundary order zero away from that boundary. For an ambient boundary restricted to a smooth closed support, use its actual pulled-back ideal on that support. This definition makes no finiteness assertion.

source.place: Bierstone--Milman, Functoriality in resolution of singularities, Publ. RIMS 44 (2008), Definitions 2.1--2.5 and Theorems 6.1--6.2, pp.618--620,629--633; publisher full text https://ems.press/content/serial-article-files/41043; numerical input cited by ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13.
